author: Reuters
description:
Kevin Warsh’s predecessor had been investigated over cost overruns related to central bank renovation project

The US ⁠justice department is not reopening a criminal investigation into former Federal Reserve chair Jerome Powell ⁠for cost overruns ⁠related ​to the central bank’s building renovation project, a department spokesperson said on Friday.

Attorney general Todd ⁠Blanche – in comments to Bloomberg News, which first reported the development – said he has not ruled out ⁠continuing to look into the project’s oversight and potentially take ​action if evidence of ‌wrongdoing came to ‌light.

Continue reading...
title: DoJ declines to reopen investigation into former Fed chair Jay Powell

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Kenan ‘Ken’ Urker, 34, who died of apparent drug overdose, was partner of woman convicted of murder of mother

The on-and-off partner of Gypsy Rose Blanchard, who spent time in prison for her role in the murder of her abusive mother, was found dead inside his Louisiana home on his 34th birthday on Thursday in what authorities described as an apparent drug overdose.

The sheriff’s office in Lafourche parish, Louisiana, confirmed Kenan “Ken” Urker – the father of Blanchard’s daughter – was discovered on Thursday after relatives asked police to conduct a welfare check at his residence.

Continue reading...
title: Partner of Gypsy Rose Blanchard found dead in Louisiana home

author: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro
description:
President leads huge rally in Rio before election on Sunday seen as most important for decades

The Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has claimed he is the only thing standing in the way of far-right “fascists” reclaiming power, as he led a huge rally through the streets of Rio ahead of Sunday’s crunch election.

Speaking on the eve of the demonstration, the 80-year-old leftwinger said he had decided to seek a historic fourth term because he believed only he could prevent the family of his rightwing rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, returning to government.

Continue reading...
title: Brazil’s Lula says only he can stop rise of fascism under Bolsonaro’s son

author: Adria R Walker in Jackson, Mississippi
description:
Dozens of residents testify to legislature’s redistricting committee in heated hearing, the last of eight

Hundreds of people gathered across from the Mississippi state capitol building on Thursday evening to rally against the aggressive Republican efforts to draw maps that favor their own party.

Shortly after the US supreme court’s decision in Louisiana v Callais, which severely weakened section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, Tate Reeves, the Mississippi governor, moved in lockstep with other Republican governors and lawmakers to call for a special session to redraw maps. However, before that special session could occur, Reeves canceled it and wrote on X that he expected “lawmakers to redraw congressional lines BETWEEN NOW and 2027 elections!”

Continue reading...
title: Hundreds gather in Mississippi to protest Republican redistricting: ‘This fight is familiar territory’

author: Lucy Campbell
description:
Hōlei sea arch, formed 550 years ago by erosion from ocean waves, no longer standing, National Park Service confirms

A famed centuries-old sea arch on Hawaii’s remote and rugged coastline has collapsed into the Pacific Ocean, the National Park Service confirmed on Friday, following a stretch of rough storms in the region in recent weeks.

The beloved landmark, Hōlei sea arch, stood at around 90ft high for over half a millennium in Hawaii’s Volcanoes national park, located on the dramatic southern coast of the Big Island. It was naturally formed around 550 years ago due to differential erosion by ocean waves.

Continue reading...
title: Hawaii’s centuries-old sea arch collapses into Pacific after series of rough storms

author: Martin Farrer
description:
The epicentre was at Leongatha, 130km south-east of Melbourne, with residents reporting houses shaking just after 2am

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A magnitude 4.8 earthquake struck Victoria in the early hours of Saturday morning, shaking Melbourne and waking people across the whole region.

Geoscience Australia said it detected an earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 4.8 at 2.01am near Leongatha, 130km south-east of Melbourne, with the tremors felt across the city’s eastern suburbs.

Continue reading...
title: Magnitude 4.8 earthquake hits Victoria with tremors felt across Melbourne

author: George Chidi
description:
Senate Leadership Fund is redirecting ad spending from Michael Whatley’s campaign to support other candidates

A major Republican political action committee pulled the plug on financial support for its Senate candidate in North Carolina, Michael Whatley, according to multiple reports, as the party begins to triage resources amid increasingly dire midterm polling.

The Senate Leadership Fund (SLF), the campaign arm of the Senate majority leader, John Thune, has withdrawn its ad spending in North Carolina to redirect support to other candidates, Semafor reported on Friday. The New York Times, CNN and other publications have confirmed the report with sources close to the fund.

Continue reading...
title: Republicans pull funding of Trump-backed Senate candidate in critical North Carolina race

author: Natricia Duncan
description:
Buckingham Palace say the king will not ‘shy away’ from Britain’s role in slavery when he visits Commonwealth nations later this month

King Charles III will acknowledge the “darkest days” of colonial rule and slavery while touring Caribbean countries on a visit beginning this month, a Buckingham Palace spokesperson said on Friday.

The king will first visit the Bahamas and Guyana alone, followed by a trip to Antigua and Barbuda with Queen Camilla, where Charles will give a speech at a meeting of Commonwealth heads of government, the palace said.

Continue reading...
title: King Charles III to acknowledge ‘darkest days’ of Britain’s colonial rule during Caribbean tour

author: George Chidi
description:
A Princeton researcher found that publicly available election records could be combined with AI to link voters to their ballots

When voters cast their ballots, their votes are supposed to remain secret: from their family, their neighbors, and the government.

But what if artificial intelligence could make secret votes visible?

Continue reading...
title: Georgia holds emergency meeting on AI exposing voters’ secret ballots

author: Keely Aouga
description:
Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority are now considering setting trained falcons on the urban birds

The mass transit authorities in the greater Boston region are clawing around for ways to mitigate the excessive local pigeon population – or more graphically, pigeon poo all over stations – and have swooped on the possibility of setting trained falcons on them.

The Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority (MBTA), the public system commonly known as “the T”, issued a “request for information” (RFI) last month from falconry experts on the potential use of birds of prey, such as falcons, to control the crowds of urban birds widely considered a public nuisance.

Continue reading...
title: Boston mass transit authorities flap around for solution to pigeon menace

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Mattie Music Group, owners of Bill Withers’ back catalogue, contend the Grammy winner infringed on Just the Two of Us

Olivia Dean has been accused of plagiarizing the Bill Withers classic Just the Two of Us.

The owners of Withers’ back catalogue aimed that allegation at his fellow Grammy winner in a copyright infringement lawsuit filed on Thursday in US federal court in Los Angeles.

Continue reading...
title: Olivia Dean accused of plagiarism on her I’ve Seen It track

author: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent
description:
Five defendants accused of being part of ‘black team’ tasked with overcoming security at Israel-linked firm Elbit near Bristol

Palestine Action activists brandished whips, hammers and kebab skewers to intimidate security guards and keep them at bay during a break-in at an Israel-linked arms factory, a court has heard.

Five defendants are accused by prosecutors of being part of a “black team”, wearing black jumpsuits, whose role was to overwhelm security guards, so that a “red team”, wearing red jumpsuits, could break into the Elbit systems factory in Filton, near Bristol, and smash up equipment including drones.

Continue reading...
title: Palestine Action activists used whips and hammers to threaten guards at arms factory, court hears

author: Lucy Campbell
description:
The 1938 mansion, Casa Encantada, once belonged to Conrad Hilton and was sold at foreclosure auction

Tech billionaire Peter Thiel has been revealed as the new owner of a storied Bel-Air estate that quietly sold in July for a staggering $130m.

The 1938 mansion, Casa Encantada, was sold at an open-air foreclosure auction in Pomona, with the name of the buyer kept under wraps for months. The winning bid is now revealed to have come from a limited liability company linked to the venture capitalist and PayPal and Palantir co-founder, according to the Wall Street Journal, which first reported the buyer’s identity.

Continue reading...
title: Peter Thiel revealed as secret buyer of Bel Air mansion that sold for $130m

author: Kiran Stacey and Richard Adams
description:
Exclusive: Education secretary sends Ofsted back to ‘drawing board’ as teachers raise serious concerns about new system

School inspections in England will be overhauled for the second time in a year, after a barrage of complaints that the new system was dangerously stressful and damaging teachers’ mental health.

Lucy Powell, the education secretary, will tell the schools regulator Ofsted to “go back to the drawing board” after becoming concerned that inspection changes overseen by her predecessor, Bridget Phillipson, were creating problems for headteachers.

Continue reading...
title: England school inspections to be overhauled again after barrage of complaints

author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
description:
Rolling stock companies, which also paid out nearly £400m to shareholders, accused of profiting at passengers’ expense

The chief executives of three firms that rent out trains to Britain’s railways were paid a combined £3.5m last year as they passed on almost £400m to shareholders in dividends.

Rail unions accused the rolling stock companies (Roscos) of raking in profits at passengers’ expense.

Continue reading...
title: Bosses of three firms that supply trains to UK railways made £3.5m last year

author: Jason Burke International security correspondent
description:
Questions raised over cockpit locks and screening of pilots as UAE investigates details and motives of near disaster

At around 9.30 on Wednesday morning local time, Tali Manes was taking her six-year-old daughter Nina to the toilet on the regular flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv when she heard a series of heavy blows against the cockpit door.

Manes, an Israeli bank executive, immediately told a flight attendant seated nearby that something was wrong. When he didn’t react, she shouted at him: “Something is happening in there!” Seconds later, the man “simply went to the [cockpit] door and opened it”, Manes told Israel’s Channel 12 TV.

Continue reading...
title: Aviation security back in spotlight after nightmare on flydubai flight to Israel

author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
description:
Home affairs department orders all federal government agencies to conduct review of ‘legacy technology’ amid fallout from AI agent hacks

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Australian government faces significant “tech debt” that could bring a big bill for taxpayers after the OpenAI Medicare breach, as government agencies will need to fortify their defences against future attacks by AI agents.

This week, the home affairs department ordered all federal government agencies to conduct a “legacy technology stocktake” that requires a plan for each agency to “reduce legacy technology systems”
title: OpenAI’s Medicare attack has exposed Australia’s ‘tech debt’. Fixing it could bring a big bill for taxpayers

author: Pjotr Sauer in Kyiv
description:
Mayor Vitali Klitschko says Kyivans can no longer pretend it is ‘peacetime’ amid strikes on school, hospital and bridge

  • Europe live – latest updates

Valeriya Tkachenko was dropping her son off at school in central Kyiv when the air raid alert sounded. Staff hurried the children and parents into the shelter, where the frightened lawyer spent the next two hours with her son.

“I’m scared to death all day about what could happen to my son,” she said as she emerged from the shelter, already late for work.

Continue reading...
title: ‘The enemy is tearing our city apart’: terror in Kyiv as Russia ramps up attacks

author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Mumbai
description:
Thousands gather in Mumbai with heavy police presence as concerns mount that millions will be denied voting rights

India’s youth-led Cockroach movement kicked off more nationwide protests on Friday as thousands of people gathered in Mumbai, amid mounting concerns that millions of citizens are being unfairly stripped of their vote.

The movement, which calls itself the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) and has massive support among the country’s gen Zs, returned to the streets to demand the resignation of the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar.

Continue readi
title: India’s Cockroach movement launches new protests over changes to voter roll

author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
description:
Government struggling to deal with worst crisis in months after being taken by surprise by massive demonstrations

  • Europe live – latest updates

As dozens of school pupils sat on top of a pile of wheelie bins blocking a high school entrance in north-eastern Paris, Sophia, 17, was on the frontline of the barricade, when she would normally have been attending Spanish class.

“We hope this grows into a massive youth protest movement,” said the final year baccalaureate student at Paris’s Lycée Voltaire, who did not want her real name published. She was on her second day of blocking the school entrance along with hundreds of others, ensuring all lessons were cancelled. “We just want to be listened to by the government. We’d rather stand here doing this than have to learn in poor conditions. It’s the only way to ma
title: Fires, fury and hundreds of arrests as France gripped by student protests

author: Associated Press
description:
Death toll of medical helicopter crash is now three people as two others continue to recover from injuries, authorities say

Police divers have found the body of a patient who went missing after a medical helicopter crashed into the Pacific Ocean off Catalina Island near Los Angeles, bringing the death toll to three while two other people were recovering from their injuries, the authorities said on Friday.

Divers with the Los Angeles county sheriff’s department found the victim’s body Thursday in the wreckage of the helicopter after searching more than 156 sq miles (404 sq km) over 23 hours, the Coast Guard said in a statement.

Continue reading...
title: Police divers find body of person missing after helicopter crash near LA

author: Guardian staff and agency
description:
Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez remains in custody after surgery to remove bullet supporters say was stuck close to his spine

The Venezuelan delivery driver who was shot and wounded by a federal immigration agent in Texas last month had surgery on Thursday to remove the bullet that had been lodged in his back for nearly two weeks.

Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, 28, had appeared in court in a wheelchair on Wednesday, wearing a sling on his arm. He remains in custody on charges that he assaulted an officer while trying to evade arrest.

Continue reading...
title: Man shot by ICE in Texas has surgery to remove bullet lodged in his back

author: Stephen Starr in Dayton, Ohio
description:
The case of the Siders family illustrates major shortcomings among Ohio’s political and administrative authorities

In June 2025, Jody Walker stood in front of Ohio lawmakers at a senate finance committee meeting in Columbus. As the head of South Central Ohio Job and Family Services, he was desperate for help.

“I have been a county director since 1999, yet I have not seen such a challenging time in the child welfare system as I do today,” he said, “specifically in terms of the needs of our children.”

Continue reading...
title: ‘A persistent crisis’: the 16 children removed from an Ohio family are part of a statewide issue

author: Edward Helmore in Philadelphia
description:
City on edge as police comb home of Raymond Horsch, pornographer who died last year, in grisly case involving disturbing pictures and film

A dilapidated house, burned out above the second story, may hold clues to dark tales and – potentially – the darkest of endings as the FBI and police in Philadelphia try to unpick what took place at 417 West Chew Avenue for more than three decades.

Last week, homicide investigators shifted their focus from examining an archive of a million photographs and film recovered from what is known locally as the “house of horrors” to excavating what is in or under the home of Raymond “RC” Horsch, a career criminal, local artist, author and snuff photographer who died last year aged 82, and his son Eugene, 44.

Continue reading
title: Does Philadelphia’s ‘house of horrors’ hold the key to seven missing women?

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Group says trading was helped by airing of Netflix documentary and opening of its 100th outlet

  • Business live – latest updates

The UK arm of Gordon Ramsay’s restaurants empire remained in the red last year despite sales topping £100m for the first time after a string of openings in a London tower.

The celebrity chef’s UK business, which has 34 outlets including the Savoy Grill, Pétrus and several Lucky Cat restaurants, narrowed losses to £5.8m from £9.4m the year before. Sales rose 3% to almost £101m.

Continue reading...
title: Gordon Ramsay’s UK restaurants stay in red despite sales topping £100m

author: Martin Belam
description:
Failed attempt to execute 50-year-old prompts review of state’s execution practices. Plus the California woman who is allergic to cold

Good morning. Tennessee’s governor has suspended executions as Christa Pike’s lawyer says the state’s failed lethal injection execution attempt has left her in a critical condition. Bill Lee, the Republican state governor, has suspended all executions in the state until at least the end of the year and ordered an independent inquiry.

Leading voices on the death penalty in the US have told the Guardian that the failed execution was such a violation of the constitutional prohibition on “cruel and unusual punishment” that all judicial killings should be halted nationwide.

What have Pike’s lawyers said about her c
title: Christa Pike left in ‘critical condition’ as Tennessee halts all executions | First Thing

author: Taz Ali
description:
Kathy Hochul said she no longer has faith in the local district attorney’s ability to handle the case, which has restarted a national conversation about sexual assault on college campuses

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US email

The governor of New York, Kathy Hochul, has named New York attorney general Letitia James as special prosecutor to investigate an alleged gang-rape at Cornell University in 2024, saying she had lost faith in the local district attorney’s ability to handle the case.

Both Hochul and James are due to speak today to provide an update on the investigation following the attorney general’s appointment.
title: Hochul to address Cornell University case after appointing Leticia James to investigate alleged gang-rape – US politics live

author: Jillian Ambrose
description:
Motorists and small businesses struggle with costs as Iran war drives up cost of oil worldwide

  • ‘Half my day’s pay goes to filling up my car’

  • Business live – latest updates

British motorists face more pressure at the pumps after the average price of diesel climbed to a record £2 a litre.

The price at UK forecourts has risen sharply since late February, when the US-Israel war on Iran began disrupting supplies of crude and refined oil products from the Gulf, leading to cost increases across the economy.

Continue reading...
title: UK diesel price hits record high of £2 a litre

author: Henry Belot
description:
Baird, father of former NSW premier Mike Baird and journalist Julia Baird, helped win the Olympics for Sydney

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Bruce Baird, a former federal Liberal MP and deputy leader of the party’s New South Wales branch, has died aged 84.

Baird, who also served as the NSW transport minister from 1988 to 1995, is the father of former state premier Mike Baird, the ABC journalist Julia Baird, and the marketing executive Steve Baird.

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
title: Bruce Baird, former federal Liberal MP and NSW minister, dies aged 84

author: Mark Sweney
description:
In effort to avoid panic at pumps, Keir Mather insists supply of fuel to Britain is ‘inherently resilient’

  • Business live – latest updates

The government has moved to avert panic at the pumps, insisting that the UK is not facing a diesel shortage after Donald Trump threatened to cut off US supplies of the fuel.

The transport minister Keir Mather said on Friday that the UK has a wide range of sources of the fuel and is in talks with other European countries over the potential release of emergency diesel stockpiles.
title: UK is not facing diesel shortage despite fears of Trump export ban, minister says

author: Ed Pilkington
description:
Pike alive but in critical condition as experts call ordeal that unfolded in Tennessee Wednesday ‘unimaginably barbaric’

Top lawyers, doctors and members of the faith community are calling for a moratorium on the US death penalty after Tennessee’s failed attempt to execute Christa Pike left the prisoner alive but in critical condition and receiving life-saving medical care.

The recent spate of harrowingly botched executions across US death penalty states reached a new low late on Wednesday when Tennessee’s governor Bill Lee called off the procedure after Pike had been injected with two full syringes of pentobarbital. She is the only person to have survived being administered 5mg of the sedative – a massive dose that under normal circumstances is considered fatal.
title: Calls grow for US death penalty halt after ‘torturous’ botched execution of Christa Pike

author: Megan Davies and James Michelin for MetDesk
description:
Up to 300mm of rain could fall in places, while extreme downpours bring deadly landslides to Nepal

Torrential rain and potentially damaging flooding are forecast in eastern Spain over the coming days, as cold upper air moves over the warm, humid surface air of the Mediterranean Sea, fuelling violent, slow-moving thunderstorms near Spain’s east coast. The weather pattern, known as a Dana, occurs most often in autumn.

Models show more than 100mm of rain could fall across the region on Friday, with 200-300mm possible in some areas. Cities including Valencia and Castelló de la Plana, with Valencia having experienced several damaging floods in recent years, are most at risk. Catalonia has now put three towns under lockdown and Valencia has shut schools for nearly half a million children.

Continue reading...
title: Eastern Spain braces for torrential rain and flooding

author: Jordyn Beazley
description:
Under new WA laws anyone who defies an exclusion order could face a maximum $36,000 fine and three years in prison

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Activists and a Greens MP have threatened legal action after the Western Australia police banned at least 12 people entering a designated security area where the Land Forces weapons expo will be held in Perth from 6 October.

The police used special powers given to them by the WA government last month to ban the activists from entering the area surrounding the Perth Convention and Exhibition Centre.

Continue re
title: Activists plan legal action against police ban on entering security zone near Perth weapons expo

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
Dozens of schools have been damaged and nearly 3,000 teenagers have been detained since the start of the tensions

Some 100 schools have been severely damaged during French high school protests that escalated this week into “urban violence,” with 40 headteachers injured, according to the latest figures from the French education ministry.

The pupils’ grievances range from overloaded timetables and overcrowded classes to insufficient teachers and unbearable temperatures during heatwaves earlier this year. Riot police have been deployed to confront the increasingly violent protests.

Continue reading...
title: 400 French schools closed on Friday as protests escalate into ‘urban violence’ – Europe live

author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
description:
Britain’s nursing union axes Teva UK as commercial partner over links to Israel’s military and corporate track record

Britain’s nursing union has cut its ties with an Israeli drug company over the firm’s links to the country’s military and track record of corporate misconduct.

The Royal College of Nursing (RCN) has axed Teva UK as a commercial partner and as sponsor of a forthcoming event on migraine and headaches at the union’s London headquarters.

Continue reading...
title: Royal College of Nursing cuts ties with Israeli drug company

author: Libby Brooks
description:
In today’s newsletter: When a passenger plane plunges 17,000ft amid claims of terrorism, hijacking and geopolitical intrigue, Guardian journalists have to try and separate fact from fiction in real time

Good morning. Shocking news of a cockpit stabbing. Graphic footage of bloodied crew members. Mid-air testimony from terrified passengers.

This was the tenor of the heart-in-mouth reporting as the horrifying events unfolded onboard flight FZ 1073 to Tel Aviv: the early morning budget flight that plummeted 17,000ft in under two minutes before the courageous intervention of passengers and crew averted an apparent hijacking, potentially saving the lives of not just the 170+ passengers and crew on board, but many more.

UK politics | Ministers are working up sweeping plans for welfare changes including scrapping a key di
title: Friday briefing: How we covered the flydubai incident as it unfolded

author: Mark Sweney
description:
Redundancy process suggests home of Gavin and Stacey and Fleabag could go online-only again in £500m cuts push

The BBC has started a redundancy process in its TV and streaming division, heightening staff fears that Matt Brittin will announce the closure of the poorly performing BBC Three and BBC Scotland channels next week.

The corporation’s director general, who has repeatedly said that linear TV and radio services may have to shut as audiences move online, is expected to inform staff on Wednesday of the latest stage of a plan to save £500m and shed up to 2,000 jobs.

Continue reading...
title: Staff fears grow that BBC will shut its Three and Scotland channels next week

author: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro
description:
Speculation that Flávio Bolsonaro will try to strip Our Lady of Aparecida of position could become deciding factor in run-up to Sunday

A row of Biblical proportions has erupted in the run-up to Brazil’s presidential election, with the country’s patron saint, Our Lady of Aparecida, emerging as an unlikely kingmaker in the deadlocked race.

Ahead of Sunday’s vote, the two frontrunners – the leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, and his far-right challenger, Flávio Bolsonaro – are level in the polls.

Continue reading...
title: ‘No one disrespects Our Lady’: fears for Brazil’s patron saint grip country ahead of election

author: Kat Wong
description:
Lamarre-Condon asked fellow officer if Paul Thijssen ‘would have gotten away with’ James’s murder if he hadn’t subsequently killed himself

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon asked a colleague, a day before he allegedly murdered Jesse Baird and Luke Davies, if a high-profile killer would have “gotten away with it” if he’d not taken his own life, a Sydney court has heard.

Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting the couple with his p
title: Beau Lamarre-Condon asked police investigator about murder of Lilie James day before shootings, court hears

author: Presented by Annie Kelly with Tom Phillips; produced by Guy Szafman and Brian McNamara; executive producer Sami Kent and Homa Khaleeli
description:
Latin America correspondent Tom Phillips reports on this Sunday’s historic presidential elections in Brazil, as the son of jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro hopes to take power

You would have been forgiven for thinking that when Jair Bolsonaro was convicted in September 2025 of attempting a coup, his political career was finished and his legacy forever tainted.

But in the first round of Brazil’s presidential elections this Sunday, another Bolsonaro has genuine hopes of victory – not Jair, but his son Flávio, who ialso campaigning to have his father released released.

Continue reading...
title: The Bolsonaros…they’re back! Brazil heads to the polls – podcast

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
Migration agents and lawyers ‘selling false hope’ to people seeking to stay in Australia also in ministers’ sights as they seek to reduce overseas arrivals

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

“Visa hopping” international students, migration agents and lawyers trying to “game” the migration system will be targeted by the federal government, as Labor unveils a further crackdown.

The changes announced on Friday mean international students will soon need to apply for a separate visa to
title: Labor targets ‘visa hopping’ international students in crackdown on ‘permanently temporary’ migration

author: Guardian staff and agency
description:
New York attorney general brought in by governor after recent questions raised over university’s 2024 investigation

Kathy Hochul, the New York governor, said Thursday she is appointing Letitia James, the state’s attorney general, as special prosecutor to investigate the alleged gang-rape at Cornell University.

“The young woman at the center of this case deserves to know that every fact will be examined and justice pursued,” Hochul said in a statement. “This action will ensure that the matter is fully and thoroughly investigated without conflict or bias, and handled independently with the rigor that this matter demands.”

Continue reading...
title: Letitia James appointed special prosecutor in alleged gang-rape at Cornell

author: Adeshola Ore
description:
NSW police allege the men, aged 18, 19 and 20, broke into homes in Arncliffe and Bankstown this week before assaulting the women aged 31 and 32

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Three men have been detained after two women were allegedly assaulted during separate home invasions in Sydney’s south-west.

New South Wales police were called to a home invasion in Arncliffe at about 12am on Tuesday morning.
title: Women hospitalised and three men charged with assault and choking after separate home invasions in Sydney

author: Associated Press
description:
Four astronauts pulled up at International Space Station after eight-hour express flight led by Jessica Watkins

Four astronauts pulled up at the International Space Station on Thursday after launching on an eight-hour express that set a US speed record, and that created further history with the first Black woman to lead a crew to orbit.

SpaceX launched commander Jessica Watkins and her crew for Nasa after a three-week delay to fix their Dragon capsule’s leaking fuel system. Thick clouds threatened all morning to halt the countdown but in the end, the skies cleared enough to allow for a safe liftoff.

Continue reading...
title: SpaceX flight led by first Black female commander sets US speed record

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Russia’s foreign ministry had called planned shows unacceptable due to rapper’s ‘glorification’ of Adolf Hitler

Two sold-out shows that Kanye West was due to play in Russia have been cancelled after weeks of confusion, organisers have confirmed.

The US rapper, who now goes by the name Ye, had been due to perform at the Gazprom Arena in St Petersburg on 10 and 11 October.

Press Association contributed to this report

Continue reading...
title: Kanye West’s sold-out Russia concerts cancelled, organisers confirm
